faqs.q: What is burrowing along West Union gardens and barn edges?
faqs.a: Woodchucks, most likely — the creek-bottom farms and gardens are textbook woodchuck ground. We remove the animals at the burrow, and advise on backfilling and fencing the garden line so the next woodchuck off the ridge finds it closed.

West Union.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's West Union calls follow the ground the town sits on: middle Island Creek (through town), North Bend Rail Trail (along the creek), wooded ridges surrounding the valley. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, woodchucks, bats in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

In fall and winter, squirrels and rodents push into warm attics across the county, and spring brings denning raccoons looking for chimneys and soffits to raise young. West Union is a small historic town of 1800s homes and brick blocks in the creek valley. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.

faqs.q: Why do bats roost in Smithburg-area farmhouses?
faqs.a: Quiet attics in older farmhouses near the creek's insect-rich bottoms are prime big brown bat roosts. Bat work is exclusion only, following the Division's bat exclusion guidelines — inspection any time, one-way exits timed so no flightless pups are trapped.
